requirements.evidence: Migration with the FK cascade, nullable invited_by with nullOnDelete, role default and unique(entity_id,email) (database/migrations/..._create_entity_invites_table.php:14-27). Email normalized by a model mutator (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:39-52). pending scope (EntityInvite.php:67-70). sendInvite validates, rejects members and pending invites, replaces settled rows, turns a QueryException conflict into an inviteEmail error, queues mail, writes an audit log, resets the form, and counts only successful invites against the 10/hour limit (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:61-130). PendingInvites accept is idempotent, checks expiry, claims the invite atomically and uses firstOrCreate for the membership, then sets the session and redirects (PendingInvites.php:18-66). Members page uses the manageMembers gate on mount; openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval/removeMember match the spec. Modal header uses ui.members_details, the role select has no empty option, and removal uses a confirmation modal with no wire:confirm (members.blade.php:84-147). Onboarding/switcher embed the list, and the hr only renders when invites exist (pending-invites.blade.php:4-5). Mail and translations match the quoted strings.

conventions.evidence: Positive: a new EntityInvitePolicy and a manageMembers ability on EntityPolicy, #[Fillable] set, migration has a down(), CHANGELOG, docs/business-rules.md and docs/database-schema.md updated, PHPDoc on public methods. Deviation: domain writes (create invite, accept invite with membership creation, role change, delete) are done inline in the Livewire components (Members.php:83-97, PendingInvites.php:37-51), not in app/Actions/* classes as the conventions require. memberRole has no #[Validate] attribute and is validated with an inline rules array (Members.php:184).

security.evidence: Every action re-resolves IDs inside the entity scope (invites()->findOrFail, memberships()->findOrFail) and authorizes through policies. accept/decline check that the invitee e-mail matches (EntityInvitePolicy.php:14-41). Validation runs before the rate limiter. Output is escaped with {{ }}. Lookups do not leak whether an e-mail has an account. Minor: selectedMembershipId is client-writable instead of #[Locked]. This is mitigated because selectedMembership() resolves it within the entity and fails with findOrFail (Members.php:255-258).

tests.evidence: SendInviteTest covers the happy path, invalid e-mail, the owner role, the quota not consumed by invalid input, the 10/hour limit, existing member (case-insensitive), duplicate pending, expired replacement, the race via a subclass override, and foreign cancel (404). PendingInvitesTest covers case-insensitive listing, accept, idempotency, no duplicate membership, expired, intruder accept/decline (403), onboarding with and without the hr, and the switcher. MembersTest/MemberDetailsTest cover 403 for employees, the error rendering once, demotion of the last manager, foreign membership tampering, the confirm/cancel removal flow, and a manager demoted mid-session being refused by each action. EntityInviteMailTest checks the en and pt_BR rendering and the subject.

simplicity.evidence: Extracts managerCount() to remove the duplicated query (Members.php:260-265) and reuses the pending() scope and normalizeEmail. isInviteConflict string-matches the exception message (Members.php:283-289) where Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException would be simpler and more robust.

readability.evidence: Small, focused, documented methods (memberExists, hasPendingInvite, inviteRateKey, selectedMembership). Comments explain non-obvious choices, such as dateTime vs timestamp in the migration and why pending rows are left in place. Naming is consistent with sibling components and there is no dead code.

scope.evidence: All changes serve the task: model, migration, factory, policy, components, views, mail, translations, docs and tests. The only additions beyond the contract are closeMember() and the members_remove_body key, which the modal UI needs.

issues.explanation: The conventions say domain writes go through app/Actions/* classes, but invite creation, invite acceptance with membership creation, and role changes are written inline in the Livewire components.

The unique-constraint race is detected by matching substrings in the exception message, which depends on the database driver; catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException would be simpler and more reliable.

memberRole has no #[Validate] attribute (validated inline in saveRole) and selectedMembershipId is not #[Locked]; both are mitigated by inline validation and in-entity re-resolution, but they depart from the stated Livewire policy.
cancelInvite resolves any invite of the entity, including accepted or expired rows, rather than only pending ones.
The expiry date is hard-coded to the d/m/Y format even for the English locale.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member addition with an invite flow: a new model, migration, factory and policy, the PendingInvites component on the switcher and onboarding, a queued markdown mail, and a manager-only members page with a details modal and a removal confirmation. Tests are thorough and include unauthorized and tamper cases. It meets essentially every requirement, with sound authorization and race handling. The main reservation is that the domain writes live in the Livewire components instead of app/Actions, plus fragile detection of unique-constraint errors. I would approve it with follow-ups.
